key_insight: Distal weight-bearing implants must be designed as coupled biomechanical–biomaterial systems, where geometry, graded coatings, and fixation performance jointly determine load transfer and osseointegration.
engineering_relevance: The review informs implant designers and translational engineers on how finite element gait loading, functionally graded Ti-HAp interfaces, and coating durability can be used to reduce micromotion and improve long-term distal support.
method: Systematic review of DWBI concepts, biomaterial interfaces, and clinical translation pathways
Quantitative trend analysis of 34 direct-contribution papers and 32 empirical studies
Synthesis of finite element, in-vivo osseointegration, and graded material evidence
evidence_signal: The evidence base is still early-stage: more than half of the empirical studies were bench or simulation only, with animal and clinical validation representing a smaller share.
watch_item: Graded Ti-HAp and FGM claims are supported mainly by non-DWBI analog studies, so device-level validation under patient-realistic gait loading and coating-fatigue conditions is still needed.
paper_title: Biomaterials and biomechanical design of distal weight-bearing implants: Computational modeling, biomaterial interfaces, and clinical translation
